transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, occupational health sent me here. They're saying I'm not eating enough. But honestly, most days I just have black coffee, maybe a plain yogurt, or just a few bites of chicken at night. Eating a full meal just... it feels like I'm letting my standards slip, you know?
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah, I am. If I step on the scale and it's up even half a pound, I get this... this jolt, like I've completely lost control. When that happens, I'll spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder. I just really can't stand the idea of putting weight back on.
Do you feel fat even when other people say you’re too thin?

Yeah, I do. When I look in the mirror, I just... I don't see what everyone else says they see. They might tell me I'm too thin, but I immediately focus on my stomach and my waist. Honestly, I judge my entire day by what I see right there. If I don't look lean enough, it's hard to even respect myself.
Has your weight dropped to a level that doctors have said is dangerously low for your height?

Yeah, they told me that at the clinic. I know my uniform hangs off me now, and I've had to tighten my belt past the old notches just to keep it up. But honestly, even when the nurse told me my weight was dangerously low, I just... I still thought to myself, I could stand to be a little sharper.
